mcat_description.short: A Net House is a prefabricated agricultural structure with a GI pipe or wire rope frame covered with UV-stabilised shade net or insect-proof net, sold as a turnkey protected cultivation system for farms and nurseries.
mcat_description.long: Net Houses are naturally ventilated, semi-controlled environment structures built using galvanised iron (GI) pipes, angle iron, or wire rope frames covered with HDPE or polyethylene shade nets in varying shade percentages (15%–90%), designed to regulate light intensity, temperature, and pest ingress for crop cultivation. They are available in flat roof, dome/round top, A-roof (anti-rain), wire rope (cable-purlin), and multi-span configurations, assembled with nut-bolt connections requiring no welding, making them prefabricated and field-erectable. In the Indian market, net houses are widely promoted under NHB (National Horticulture Board) and MIDH government subsidy schemes, making subsidy-model compliance a key purchase criterion for farmer-buyers. They serve as a cost-effective alternative to polyhouses for vegetables, floriculture, nursery propagation, and off-season cultivation across Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka, Rajasthan, and Gujarat.

market_context: Net Houses are the dominant low-cost protected cultivation structure in India, positioned between open-field farming and fully enclosed polyhouses; they are widely promoted under the National Horticulture Board (NHB) and Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) subsidy schemes, making subsidy-model compliance a key commercial differentiator. The Indian market recognises several distinct structural types — flat roof, dome/round top, A-roof (anti-rain), wire rope/cable-purlin, and multi-span — with GI pipe (IS 1161 grade) and hot-dip galvanised wire rope as the dominant frame materials confirmed across multiple manufacturer sources. Shade net covering is available in 15%, 35%, 40%, 50%, 75%, and 90% shade factors in HDPE or polypropylene, with 50% being the most common for vegetable cultivation; insect-proof nets (40–50 mesh) are used for pest-exclusion applications. Key manufacturing hubs include Pune/Nashik (Maharashtra), Gandhinagar/Ahmedabad (Gujarat), Jaipur (Rajasthan), and Haryana, with adoption concentrated in Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka, Rajasthan, and Gujarat. Buyers frequently conflate net houses with polyhouses in search queries ('poly house net', 'net set house'), indicating a need for clear product differentiation in listings.
